title: Hey Krishna, hey friend
hookLine: Arjuna realizes his best friend is God, and remembers every joke he ever made
carry: god can be loved as a friend

cards: Your oldest friend, the one you've known forever. You've teased them, beaten them at cards, shared a bed on a camping trip, eaten off their plate without asking, called them ridiculous nicknames.
Then one day you find out who they really are, and it's bigger than anything you ever imagined. Your first thought might not be wow. It might be: oh no.
All those jokes. All those times I treated you like just anybody. That's exactly where Arjuna is in today's verses, trembling, palms pressed together.

teach.b: Sanjaya says Arjuna bows, trembling, and speaks with a choked voice. First, praise. It's right that the world rejoices in you and loves you.
The frightened spirits flee in every direction, and the perfected ones bow. You are the first god, the ancient person, the final resting place of the universe.
You are wind, death, fire, the moon, the father of all creatures.

teach.h: A THOUSAND TIMES, ON EVERY SIDE.
teach.b: Then: bowing to you a thousand times, and again, and again. Bowing in front, bowing behind, bowing on every side. Then the confession, verses forty-one and forty-two.
Thinking you were just my friend, I called you rashly: hey Krishna, hey Yadava, hey friend. I didn't know how great you were.
Out of carelessness, or out of love, whatever disrespect I showed you as a joke, while playing, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in front of others, I ask you to forgive it, immeasurable one.

teach.h: AS A FRIEND WITH A FRIEND.
teach.b: Verse forty-four: bear with me as a father with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved. Notice: he asks not for distance, but for the closeness to hold.
And verse forty-five: I'm thrilled to have seen what no one has seen, and my mind is shaking with fear. Please, show me the form I know. Terror and praise, both at once.
And a Hindu teaching lives right here: God can be loved as a friend. The Bhagavata Purana counts sakhya, friendship, among nine forms of devotion, and teachers often name Arjuna as its example.
Many Hindus still end a puja asking pardon for any slip, then talk to God like family.

how: Arjuna's hymn of praise in Gita 11.36–46 is recited by many Hindus in worship; sakhya, loving God as a friend, is one of the nine forms of devotion in the Bhagavata Purana, and many Hindus close a puja with a prayer asking pardon for any mistake or disrespect.

o: a servant who serves a master
a disciple who follows a guru

games.q: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.
p: as a friend with a friend

s: Arjuna asks Krishna to keep his distance from now on
verse 44: bear with me as a father with a son, a friend with a friend.
Arjuna asks forgiveness for jokes made while eating and resting
verse 42: while playing, resting, sitting or eating, alone or with others.
Arjuna feels only joy at the vision
verse 45: he's thrilled, and his mind is shaking with fear.

games.q: you've just seen that your closest friend is the whole universe. what do you do?
o: ask forgiveness for every careless word, and ask the friendship to hold.
keep a respectful distance from now on.
games.why: he asks forgiveness, and asks for closeness: as a father with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved.

practice: If you pray, speak to God for a minute the way Arjuna once did: plainly, as a friend, by whatever name is yours. Then, as many Hindus do at the end of puja, ask pardon for any careless word, and ask the closeness to stay.
If you don't pray, do the same in your heart for someone you've treated like just anybody.

wordCard.voice: Sakha. Friend, companion. Sakhya, friendship with God, is one of the forms of devotion. Seeing his friend as God, he bows a thousand times, and asks forgiveness for every careless word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: sakha, friend, companion; 'he sakhe', hey friend, is one of the names Arjuna regrets (11.41).

carryVoice: Your line: God can be loved as a friend. Hey Krishna, hey friend: the names he used before he knew. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 11.41–11.46 (forgive my familiarity; show me the form I know)
Bhagavata Purana 7.5.23 (the nine forms of devotion, including sakhya)
